title: Teeth whitening
what: The dentist puts a special gel on your teeth that lightens the enamel by a few shades.
why: When you want lighter teeth, for example after staining from coffee, tea, or smoking.
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Whitening is usually postponed
If you have fillings or crowns on your front teeth. They do not get lighter

prepare.title: Cleaning
prepare.text: A professional cleaning is usually done first, often a few days before whitening.

prepare.title: Treatment
prepare.text: Cavities and sore gums are treated first. Only healthy teeth are whitened.

prepare.title: Expectations
prepare.text: Ask your dentist how much lighter your own teeth will get. Results differ for everyone.

bring: Headphones, if you want to listen to music
steps: The dentist checks the current shade of your teeth with a color guide
A lip retractor is put in to hold your lips back
Your gums are covered with a protective gel
Whitening gel is put on your teeth
Sometimes a lamp is shone on the gel
The gel is changed a few times, then rinsed off
The shade before and after is compared
feel: The lip retractor makes your lips tired
Sometimes short, sharp twinges in the teeth
Afterward, your teeth may be sensitive to cold for 1 to 3 days
after: For 1 to 2 days, follow a white diet: no coffee, tea, wine, berries, beets, sauces, or smoking
You can use toothpaste for sensitive teeth if your dentist advises it
Results usually last from 6 months to a few years, depending on your habits

faq.q: Is whitening bad for my teeth?
faq.a: If it is done by a dentist on healthy teeth, usually not. Short-term sensitivity is common and goes away on its own.

faq.q: Do fillings and crowns get whiter?
faq.a: No. They stay the same color. Sometimes they are replaced later to match the new shade of your teeth.

faq.q: What should I avoid eating after whitening?
faq.a: For 1 to 2 days, avoid coffee, tea, wine, brightly colored berries, and sauces, and do not smoke.
